# Copilot instructions for this repo

See `plan.md` at the repo root for the full design/architecture plan. Keep it
up to date as the source of truth when the approach changes.

## Environment
- Python 3, dependencies managed via a project-local `.venv` — **never**
  install packages into the global/system Python.
- Use `./setup.sh` to create `.venv` and install `requirements.txt`. Re-run
  after editing `requirements.txt`. Linux/macOS only — no Windows support is
  planned; Windows users should use Adobe Acrobat's own tools instead.
- Runtime deps go in `requirements.txt`; build/test-only tools (e.g.
  `pytest`, `pyinstaller`) go in `requirements-dev.txt`, kept separate so
  end users installing the packaged app don't need them.

## The `examples/` folder is third-party IP — handle with care
- `examples/` contains real, copyrighted TTRPG publishers' PDFs (D&D 5E,
  Brancalonia, STA, ION HEART, etc.). It is git-ignored on purpose.
- **Never commit anything from `examples/` to git, and never reference it
  from automated tests or CI.** It exists only for local, manual
  smoke-testing by a developer's own copies.
- Any test that needs a fillable PDF or a portrait image must use the
  original, IP-free fixtures under `tests/fixtures/` (generated by
  `tests/fixtures/generate_fixtures.py`), not files from `examples/`.

## Testing
- Automated tests live in `tests/` and run via `pytest`, using only the
  committed synthetic fixtures in `tests/fixtures/`.
- Tests must be fully self-contained and safe to run on public CI/forks —
  no dependency on locally-provided real sheets or portraits.
- GitHub Actions runs the test suite on every push/PR
  (`.github/workflows/test.yml`); keep it green and don't add steps that
  require secrets or third-party copyrighted assets.

## Packaging
- Linux distribution artifacts (`.deb`, `.rpm`, AppImage) are built from a
  PyInstaller-frozen binary via scripts under `packaging/` — see the
  "Distribution / Packaging" section of `plan.md` before changing build
  scripts, versioning (`VERSION` file), or packaging metadata.

## Dependency updates
- `.github/dependabot.yml` keeps `pip` and `github-actions` dependencies
  updated on a **monthly** cadence. Don't change this to weekly/daily
  without discussion — monthly is intentional to keep PR noise low.

## Code structure & maintainability
- The tool is a small package (`update_portrait/`) with one concern per
  module (`cli.py`, `fields.py`, `image_prep.py`, `pdf_ops.py`,
  `errors.py`) plus a thin root-level `update_portrait.py` shim — not one
  large flat script. Keep new logic in the appropriately-scoped module
  rather than piling everything into `cli.py`.
- Use type hints and a short docstring on every public function/module.
  Prefer small, pure functions (no I/O) for logic like field-name matching
  or image-fit math, so they're easy to unit test in isolation.
- Raise the custom exceptions in `errors.py` (e.g. `NoCandidateFieldError`,
  `AmbiguousFieldError`) from the logic layer; only `cli.py` should catch
  them and turn them into user-facing stderr messages/exit codes.
- Avoid magic numbers/strings — use named module-level constants (e.g. the
  field-name heuristics list, default fit mode, JPEG quality).
- Tests mirror the module layout (`tests/test_fields.py`,
  `tests/test_image_prep.py`, etc.) in addition to the fixture-driven
  end-to-end test — see "Code organization & maintainability" in `plan.md`
  for full detail.

## Project artwork — human-only
- Project artwork/branding (e.g. the AppImage/desktop icon under
  `packaging/appimage/icon.png`, or any future logo/branding asset) must
  only be created or edited by a human — **do not generate or modify these
  as an AI**.
- AI-generated imagery is fine for **test fixtures only**: simple
  programmatically-drawn shapes/gradients/patterns (e.g.
  `tests/fixtures/portrait.jpg`) used purely to exercise the image-handling
  code are not "artwork" and remain acceptable to create/edit as an AI.

## Git operations — AI limits
- **AI must never run `git commit` or `git push`** in this repo. Prepare/
  stage changes and let the human review and commit/push themselves.
- Before running any `git checkout`/`git restore`/`git reset` (or similar)
  that would discard uncommitted local changes, **stop and confirm with the
  user first** — never silently blow away someone's in-progress work.

## General conventions
- Keep the CLI (`update_portrait.py`) dependency-light: `PyMuPDF` for PDF
  handling, `Pillow` for image prep, stdlib `argparse` for the CLI — avoid
  adding new dependencies without updating `plan.md` and `requirements.txt`.
- Prefer updating `plan.md` alongside any significant design change so it
  stays an accurate record of intended architecture.
